verdict.reasoning: Transcript: doctor says, “it says here, um, you are feeling hot, and have had severe headaches. Is that correct?” but later clarifies, “you’re feeling hot, but you didn’t mention that. Is that correct?” Patient instead reports shortness of breath. Feeling hot is not confirmed; only severe headaches are.

Transcript: headaches are described as frontal and occurring at work: “No, it's mostly in the front… mostly when I'm, at work… I'm at work, I'm in a meeting, or on my laptop.” This supports frontal, episodic headaches during meetings/computer use.
Transcript: “do you feel sick?” Patient: “not, not, not really, but it's like… I kind of feel a little bit nauseous maybe.” This supports mild nausea with headaches.
Transcript: “But it, it started roughly when I changed jobs.” This refers to onset of symptoms including headaches, supporting that headaches began around the job change.
Transcript: “And, do you normally get headaches, before all of this started?” Patient: “No, I… feel like my… health situation was mostly under control.” This supports no prior history of headaches.

Palpitations: “you mentioned that you noticed your heart beating?… how often…? Patient: ‘maybe once a day.’ Shortness of breath at rest: “do you feel short of breath while you're sitting at your desk?… yes.” Tingling: “both” hands/arms; no legs. Appetite/weight loss: “you also mentioned your reduced appetite… Have you lost weight?… Five pounds… It's not intentional.” Libido: “I do have like, some loss of libido at home… since I changed my job.” All listed symptoms match.

Transcript confirms stress level “seven, or eight” and that headaches occur at work, but nowhere explicitly states work stress is a trigger for the headaches. Inferring causality (trigger) goes beyond what is said.

Transcript: Patient: “well I have, hyperthyroidism.” Doctor later: “probably do some blood tests, for your thyroxine.” Hyperthyroidism is overactive thyroid; thyroxine is used for hypothyroidism. The fact labels it as hyperthyroidism but transcript plus thyroxine use suggests hypothyroidism, creating a clinical inconsistency.
Transcript: “do you take medications for that? Patient: ‘Thyroxine.’” This supports that the patient is taking thyroxine.

Transcript: “I'm a lawyer.” “And, do you work in London at the moment? Patient: ‘Yes.’” Alcohol: “Like, once a week, couple of glasses, of wine.” Smoking: “How about smoking? Patient: ‘No.’” Drugs: “do you do anything else recreational…? Patient: ‘No.’” All elements are present.

No diagnostic assessment in transcript states headaches are likely stress/tension related or to rule out metabolic/endocrine causes. The doctor only recommends exam and blood tests without giving this interpretation.
Transcript does not attribute palpitations or shortness of breath to anxiety or thyroid issues. This is an interpretive assessment not stated by the clinician.
While bilateral hand tingling is described, the doctor does not comment on its etiology. Saying its cause is “unclear” is an added assessment not present in the transcript.

The transcript notes unintentional weight loss, decreased appetite, and decreased libido but does not state that they “need further work-up,” even though a clinic visit is planned. That phrasing is an added interpretive statement.

Transcript: “well I have, hyperthyroidism… do you take medications for that? Patient: ‘Thyroxine.’… ‘probably do some blood tests, for your thyroxine.’” Control status is not discussed, so “unknown control status” correctly reflects missing information.

Transcript: “come and see, one of our doctors, in the clinic. We can give you an examination, and… check your heart and your breathing.” Cardiac and respiratory are mentioned; neurological exam is not, so including neurological makes this an addition.
Transcript: “And probably do some blood tests, for your thyroxine.” This supports ordering thyroid-related blood tests (thyroid function tests).
The clinician does not state to continue or change thyroxine; only mentions checking blood tests. “Continue current thyroxine until review” is not in the transcript.

Transcript: “you can book an appointment through the app… I'll let them know what you've told me today, so you won't have to repeat exactly what you've said.” This matches booking via app and providing handover to the attending clinician.
